title: Ann Hui to Receive Busan Film Festival’s Camellia Award
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All August 10, 2026 9:34pm Ann Hui Busan Film Festival Ann Hui , the Hong Kong New Wave pioneer whose films have chronicled the lives of her city’s ordinary and overlooked for nearly half a century, will receive the 2026 Camellia Award at the Busan International Film Festival , presented in partnership with Chanel. The 79-year-old director will accept the prize — awarded to filmmakers who have advanced the standing of women in the industry — at the festival’s opening ceremony on Oct. 6 at the Busan Cinema Center. “In my previous years I felt unwilling to receive such taking-stock prizes because I wished to continue making movies,” Hui said in a statement. “Now that I’m nearly eighty and find it difficult to make a film, I think the prize comes just in time for me to appreciate it more.” Related Stories Movies James Gray Rejects Men Not Being "Allowed to Engage With the Tender Side" Movies Keke Palmer, Deepa Mehta, Jacob Tremblay, and Jeremy Irons Projects Set for TIFF Financing Market Since her 1979 debut The Secret , Hui has directed 27 features and two feature-length documentaries. Her work helped define the Hong Kong New Wave, with films that move across genres but return to her perennial theme — the struggles of everyday life at the margins, portrayed without sentiment: Vietnamese refugees in Boat People (1982), a daughter’s reckoning with her Japanese mother in Song of the Exile (1990), the small dignities of working-class life in The Way We Are (2008), an aging servant and the family she raised in A Simple Life (2011). Hui is already one of the most decorated directors of her generation. She has won best director at the Hong Kong Film Awards six times, more than any filmmaker in the ceremony’s history, and three times at Taiwan’s Golden Horse Awards. Twice — with Summer Snow in 1995 and A Simple Life in 2011 — her work swept best film, director, actor and actress at the Hong Kong awards. In 2020, she became the first female director to receive Venice’s Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement, sharing that year’s honor with Tilda Swinton. She was previously honored in Busan in 2014 as the Asian Filmmaker of the Year. Established in 2024, the Camellia Award takes its name from a flower that is both Busan’s civic emblem and, famously, Gabrielle Chanel’s favorite. Korean production designer Ryu Seong-hie ( Oldboy , Decision to Leave ) was its inaugural recipient, followed last year by Taiwanese actress and filmmaker Sylvia Chang. “I am so happy to return to Busan,” Hui added, “and meet an audience that is among the most savvy and cinematically literate in the world.” Hui will be honored alongside Michelle Yeoh, this year’s Asian Filmmaker of the Year, at a ceremony hosted by Pachinko star Kim Minha. The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15. THR

title: Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback Jerry Katzman Dies: Former WMA President Was 89 Caitríona Balfe Stars In Alfonso Cuarón Horror Thriller Series ‘Ascension’ Ordered By Apple TV View All August 10, 2026 9:23pm 'Newlyweds: (l-r) Tea Leoni as Jeanie, Tim Daly as James Nicole Weingart/NBC NBC did some method casting on its comedy pilot Newlyweds earlier this year, with Tèa Leoni and Tim Daly , who had tied the knot just months prior, tapped as the titular leads in the multi-camera comedy. It marked an on-screen reunion of the duo who also played a husband and wife on the 2014 CBS drama series Madam Secretary. The joint casting was not an accident. “We were kind of sniffing around to play together again,” Leoni said at NBCUniversal’s Backlot Pass event ahead of Newlyweds’ series debut this fall. “We had a lot of fun on Madam Secretary . The world got darker, and we wanted to get lighter. We thought we’ve done this particular medium, and loved it, and we wanted to spend our days together.” Related Stories News 'Newlyweds' Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She "Begged" Her Agents To Get Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Sitcoms Are Primed For Comeback Casting Damon Wayans To Guest Star On NBC's 'St. Denis Medical' Season 3 Premiere In 'In Living Color' Reunion; First-Look Photo Added Daly, “Listen, we spent six years pretending to be married on TV, and I would get to do it again, but we actually are married. It’s a miracle, it’s really fun, it’s cool, and we still like each other.” Watch on Deadline Said Leoni, “It took 12 years, but we got there.” Newlyweds tells the story of a free‑spirited woman (Leoni) and a buttoned‑up professor (Daly) who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. “We’ve been told that we have chemistry, we were told that on Madam Secretary, and, hopefully, we exported that into this show,” Daly said. Added Leoni, “We haven’t lost it.” While they have proven to have an on-screen couple chemistry, being a couple in real life has its advantages too. “One, we don’t need an intimacy coordinator because we are licensed to do whatever we want,” Daly said. Additionally, “We get to start ahead of the game,” Leoni said, giving an example with an exchange between their characters on their first date in the Newlyweds pilot. “I was looking at James, aka Tim, and I can read him, I know where he’s going,” Leoni said. “We just found this moment because ‑‑ maybe that happened somewhere else, but it happens in our life all the time, and it’s fun. It’s really fun to act with someone that you know so well because we are a little ahead with each other. It’s great, we like it.” Daly has the rare distinction of playing the love interest on two multi-camera comedies, NBC’s Newlyweds and Netflix’s Leanne, whose second season premieres later this month. Now that he has his own series, Daly is not sure whether he would continue on Leanne Morgan’s sitcom, where he has been recurring, if it’s renewed for a third season. “Netflix is its own bizarre kind of universe, so I don’t know what they are thinking about or deciding or even if I’m legally allowed to do any more of that show,” he said. NBCUniversal “Backlot Pass Day” (l-r) Gail Lerner, Jamie Lee Curtis , Bill O’Neill, Tim Daly, Téa Leoni, Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio at the Universal Studios Lot on Monday, August 10, 2026 Newlyweds is created and executive produced by Gail Lerner and Jaimie Lee Curtis, with the Oscar winner also recurring on the show. Curtis was asked about being a boss on the show. “I like to refer to myself as the ‘HBIC,’ head bitch in charge,” she said. “I’m 68 years old, I have wanted to be a boss my whole life. If you ask my children, my husband, they would tell you I’ve been a boss my whole life, but I’ve been waiting my whole life, literally, to be able to manifest ideas and bring what I love about what I do into the workplace I do it in. I’ve been doing it not as a boss for a long, long time, and now I’m a boss, and I love it.” Curtis’ choice of title was clearly by design. When asked what she brings of herself to her role as James’ (Daly) ex-wife, she had a quick response. “I’m really a bitch,” she quipped. title: ‘Camp Rock 3’ Director on Bringing the Jonas Brothers Back — and Those Surprise Star Cameos
full_text: Skip to main content From left: Liamani Segura and Malachi Barton in 'Camp Rock 3.' Disney/David Astorga Logo text [This story contains spoilers from Camp Rock 3. ] It’s been 16 years since viewers got their last look at Camp Rock. Disney Channel’s two Camp Rock films, starring the Jonas Brothers and Demi Lovato , were released in 2008 and 2010. They made a star out of Lovato and gave the Jonas Brothers — Kevin, Joe and Nick — even more exposure and fueled their rise to global superstars. Camp Rock and Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam rank among the Top 10 Disney Channel Original Movies of all time. Related Stories TV 'Camp Rock 3' Surprise! Demi Lovato Reprises Role as Mitchie in Disney's Movie TV 'Descendants' Franchise Expands With Movie Featuring Iconic Disney Sidekicks Now, Disney Channel and Disney+ are reviving the franchise with Camp Rock 3, which finds the Jonas Brothers returning as the band Connect 3, who are now looking for a new opening act. Of course, they head back to Camp Rock to discover the next big thing. Hot up-and-comers (and Disney favorites) Liamani Segura ( Descendants : Wicked Wonderland ) and Malachi Barton ( Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires ) star in the new movie, along with Lumi Pollack, Sherry Cola, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Brooklynn Pitts and Ava Jean. And Maria Canals-Barrera reprises her role as Connie, mom to Mitchie Torres, played by Lovato in the first two films. From left: Liamani Segura, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Malachi Barton and Lumi Pollack in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Veronica Rodriguez (Disney’s The Slumber Party) , who directed the movie, says she made a conscientious effort to strike a balance between keeping the tone of the original films while also updating the sensibility for today’s audience. “Even when I first went out to be the director of this movie, I knew immediately that that was going to be my Mount Everest,” she says. “I needed to make a movie that simultaneously satisfied the new Camp Rockers and the nostalgia campers like myself who grew up with the franchise and know it and love it so much and hold it as a beloved piece of DCOM [Disney Channel Original Movies] canon, just really threading that needle of making a movie that is enjoyable and fun.” She began thinking of the movie as “ Camp Rock Plus. ” “I wanted to take everything we know and love about the original Camp Rock movies and ‘plus’ them up in every way that I could,” which meant everything from the costumes to the characters. “These are kids in the arts,” she continues. “I wanted them to have a personality in how they dressed and their personalities.” From left: Kevin Jonas , Joe Jonas and Nick Jonas in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Part of that effort was also reflected in the musical numbers, which feature everything from big group dances to quieter acoustic tunes. “Even the musical numbers, I wanted to ‘plus’ those up a bit and not have off of them just be the kids dancing around the campground,” Rodriguez adds. “I was like, how can I make those feel different and have each one be unique?” To that end, the songs incorporate several musical genres, she notes, which is a reflection of the pop charts themselves that also feature a variety of genres. (The soundtrack will be released Friday, while Barton and Segura also will be performing some of these songs on the upcoming Worlds Collide Concert Tour, featuring stars from the Descendants, Zombies and Camp Rock franchises.) Given how the Jonas Brothers and Lovato’s careers blew up after the release of the first movie, Rodriguez expects the same thing to happen with Segura and Barton, who are already wildly popular with the tween crowd. Segura “is on the Demi [Lovato] track,” she says. “That girl has the voice of an angel and a heart of gold and talent beyond measure.” Barton, meanwhile, is going to be “the next Zac Efron,” she predicts, adding that he learned to play guitar for Camp Rock 3 . “The cast is insanely talented.” Demi Lovato with the Jonas Brothers in Disney’s 2008 musical film Camp Rock . Bob D’amico/©Disney Channel/Courtesy Everett Collection Speaking of Lovato, she makes a surprise appearance in the film, which has been kept top secret until now. We won’t spoil more about her appearance here, but Rodriguez said there were thoughtful discussions with Lovato, who also served as an executive producer, about how to bring Mitchie back while not taking away from the newer generation of stars. “We wanted to find the right balance of how much she should be in the film and what Mitchie’s involvement looked like,” Rodriguez says. “Her character literally says in the movie, to her mom, ‘This isn’t about me, it’s about them. It’s their time to shine. This is the new generation of campers.’ With Mitchie and Connect 3, we wanted them to be ingrained and necessary for the story but also leave enough room and space for the world to fall in love with the new generation of campers.” Another surprise star cameo comes in the form of Zombies franchise alum (and Barton’s co-star in the fourth movie) Milo Manheim , who turns up as a songwriting pro helping to instruct the campers. “Milo passed the Zombies torch to Malachi, and they’re buds,” Rodriguez says. “We were over the moon when it ended up working out for Milo to come play with us. It’s a really fun, meaningful cameo.” She said it was also heartwarming to see Manheim, along with the Jonas Brothers and Lovato, helping to mentor the younger talent on-set, such as guiding them on how to navigate social media. The Jonas Brothers also were executive producers on the movie, and Rodriguez says they were “very hands-on” throughout the process, including the production and creative on a song that Connect 3 performs in the movie. Fans of the original will likely spot some throwbacks to the first two films. Cola, who plays Connect 3’s tour manager, lands a funny line during a hip-hop class that calls back to the original (hint: it has something to do with hats), while Mitchie’s songwriting book introduced in the first film plays a role in the story. In addition, the antagonist of the story, Maddie (played by Ava Jean), was modeled in the vein of Tess (Meaghan Martin) from the original movies, giving “the most lovable mean girl vibes that take us back to the past,” Rodriguez adds. Rodriguez was also happy to bring Canals-Barrera back for a third go-round. The camp’s former head cook and Mitchie’s mom is now the camp director: “She’s the ultimate camp mom.” After the first table read, “everyone in the room loved it and we put more Connie in the movie because she brings such good energy.” From left: Maria Canals-Barrera and Liamani Segura in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Today’s audience is quite different from that of 16 years ago. Rodriguez says there was a conscious choice to incorporate what kids today are dealing with, including a scene showing the campers having their phones taken away so they can be more present. “I am a very big proponent of face-to-face communication, hanging out with your friends together, not on devices,” she says. “My hope is that kids watch this, and they like want to go jam with their friends in person and listen to music and sing and dance and just create, create memories. As amazing as technology can be, sometimes just that human-to-human, friend-to-friend, kid-to-kid interaction that can be life-changing.” Rodriguez is excited for fans to watch the movie. “It was such an honor to be able to bring back a beloved franchise like this, and I did not take that responsibility lightly,” she says. “I gave this movie a lot of care and heart and, you know, effort and love. Everyone involved really worked hard and I think succeeded in making a movie that will satisfy all generations. It just feels like pure joy.” Camp Rock 3 premieres at 8 p.m. ET/PT Thursday on Disney Channel and the next day on Disney+. Watch the trailer below. Rodriguez directs from a script by Eydie Faye. The movie is produced by Disney Kids & Family and features choreography by Jamal Sims. Tim Federle executive produces, along with the Jonas brothers, Lovato, Betsy Sullenger, Spencer Berman and Gary Marsh, with a “special thanks” to Alan Sacks for his contribution to the Camp Rock franchise. THR

title: Reggie Bannister Dies: ‘Phantasm’ Actor Was 80

According to Bannister’s wife, the actor had been exposed to Agent Orange while serving in the U.S. military during the Vietnam War. title: ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback Jerry Katzman Dies: Former WMA President Was 89 View All August 10, 2026 4:55pm L-R: Jamie Lee Curtis and Tea Leoni in NBC's 'Newlyweds' Nicole Weingart/NBC) Jamie Lee Curtis had just wrapped a movie when, during the 1988 pilot season, ABC offered her a half-hour multi-camera pilot. She did it and loved it, so she was bummed when the network didn’t pick it up to series that May. Curtis went to do another movie, and, while she was filming, A Fish Called Wanda came out in July 1988, making her an overnight global star. Suddenly, ABC called and told her they wanted to pick up that pilot, which became Anything But Love , a sitcom starring Curtis and comedian Richard Lewis that ran for four seasons. Related Stories News NBC Sets Fall Premiere Dates For ‘Chicago’ And ‘Law & Order’ Shows, ‘The Voice,’ Comedies, New Series & More News Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy “It was my favorite job I’ve ever had,” Curtis recalled during a panel Monday for the new NBC multi-camera comedy Newlyweds , which she executive produces and recurs on. “And I’m 68 years old, and every single year, all I’ve ever said to my agents is ‘I want to do a sitcom, all I want to do is a sitcom.’ It’s my favorite job, I love the whole part of it, every aspect of it, the dance with the cameras, the idea that you actually get to rehearse something and work it and learn a joke and play it. I just never got to do it, and so I just decided to basically kind of create my own job. I met Gail, and that’s why we are all here.” Gail Lerner is Newlyweds ‘ writer and executive producer. Curtis has done single-camera comedy series over the years, including New Girl and The Bear , but is not a fan of the form. “I’m telling you, I have begged my agents ‑‑ and by the way, I did a single‑camera, which I hate. I mean, great show, New Girl , very funny,” she said. “It’s a good show, but doing it is just like doing a movie. You’ve got a camera crew, and nobody laughs. They are silent, and it’s awful, for me, awful. Single‑camera comedy is not fun.” Jamie Lee Curtis on “begging” to do a multi-cam sitcom after ‘New Girl’ pic.twitter.com/AYjVYbEeZp — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 10, 2026 Like Curtis, Newlyweds stars Téa Leoni and Tim Daly also have multi-camera sitcom experience though for Leoni, it was not love at first sight. “When I did Flying Blind and Naked Truth, they used to hang air‑sickness bags behind all of the sets because I used to hurl before I came out, I used to be so scared,” she said. “In that time since I did that, I missed it, and I realized that I’m old enough, I’m tough, like, I’m good, I can do this, I want to. it’s still a little scary but it is so much fun.” Daly chimed in to “slightly dispute the characterization that people in general think [sitcoms are] old‑fashioned,” noting that young people come to him to talk about his classic sitcom Wings which they had discovered and loved. “So I think that there is an audience; it’s just a matter of us finding them and them finding us, and, hopefully, they will,” he said. Newlyweds is a later‑in‑life love story about a free‑spirited woman (Leoni) and a buttoned‑up professor (Daly) who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. Curtis plays the professor’s ex-wife, “a bitch,” in her own words. Curtis, an Oscar winner who is married to filmmaker Christopher Guest, spoke about the genesis of the idea for Newlyweds. “The truth of the matter is I met my husband and married him after seeing his picture in a magazine, and we had never spent more than 72 hours together before we got married, I mean at one time,” she said. “I think you can know what we did for the other 70 hours, there wasn’t a lot of talking. We were strangers when we married, and then you wake up one day and go, like, ‘Wow. He really doesn’t talk.'” Continued Curtis, “We have been married for 42 years, thank you very much. But the point is that there’s always been that aspect of my relationship with my husband, we are polar opposites, and that was when we started talking about a later‑in‑life thing that happens to people in their 60s, who hook up and kind of go, ‘You know what, let’s do this.’ There’s something really delicious about watching people figure out life when they are filled in a life with other people, and that’s ultimately what we kind of wanted the show to be.” L-R: Gail Lerner, Jamie Lee Curtis, Bill O’Neill, Tim Daly, Téa Leoni, Emma Meisel and Ignacio Diaz-Silverio during NBC’s “Backlot Pass Day” on Monday at the Universal Studios lot Lerner, who co-created Newlyweds with Curtis, revealed how she and NBC got involved. “Jamie brought me this idea during the pandemic, so we’ve been really generating it for a very long time. And for a million various reasons, it was hibernating for a while, and a lot of people say my project died, but I just knew my project was hibernating,” she said. “And then NBC called in November of 2025 and said, ‘Hey, let’s do that show,’ and we were off to the races.” Lerner gave NBC props for “reinvesting in multi-cam and bringing back Must See TV.” Curtis stressed the fact that Newlyweds is on a broadcast network that is accessible to anyone. “It’s also must-see free TV,” she said. “You have to remember, a lot of people don’t have any money anymore, people are really struggling, and cable and all of the things you have to spend money on. This is network television, and I actually think this whole nostalgia of what sitcoms bring you into your house, things do come around. And my guess is that NBC’s decision to pick up a show that’s going to make a block of comedy on Friday nights ‑‑ ‘Fridays: We Are In Love On NBC’ — I mean, that’s an advertising feed. That’s how you build something.” ‘Newlyweds’ EP Jamie Lee Curtis on NBC taking a chance on sitcoms and their hopes to bring a “feel good” show to viewers pic.twitter.com/HeaPJzObAZ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 10, 2026 The Friday sitcom block Newlyweds will be part of is anchored by the Reba McEntire comedy Happy’s Place . NBC set a goal this past development season to find a companion for its breakout multi-camera hit, greenlighting two pilots, one of which, Newlyweds, went to series . “The reason we are here is because Happy’s Place became such a happy place, and people wanted to go there that they needed to pair it with a show about love and friendship,” Curtis said. “I just think people want to have a good time in the comfort of their own home, and they want to turn on a network show and have laughs and have feelings. If that isn’t what sitcoms can do well, then I’m not sure what they do. That’s what they do, and that’s why we love them.” With multi-camera comedy in retreat across broadcast, Curtis hopes Newlyweds will help the genre make a comeback that will extend beyond Fridays on NBC. “My guess is then Thursdays are going to start being that, and the next thing you know, NBC is going to look like they were geniuses of bringing back the thing that real people really want, and they want it for free,” she said. “They want to turn their television on and have that level of entertainment and laughter and a good feeling about who we are as a society. And I just think that it’s exciting that we get to do, and we are grateful to NBC for doing it.” Jacob Elordi Circling Ari Aster’s A24 Film Starring Scarlett Johansson Cal AG Bonta Claims Ellison Misinformation, Side Deals In WBD Merger Caitríona Balfe Leads Alfonso Cuarón Horror Series ‘Ascension’ Ordered By Apple TV Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Now India’s Biggest Ever Hollywood Pic Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Jon Cypher Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’ Police Chief, ‘Major Dad’ Regular & ‘Masters Of The Universe’ Ally Was 94
full_text: Skip to main content By Erik Pedersen Erik Pedersen Managing Editor More Stories By Erik Jon Cypher Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’ Police Chief, ‘Major Dad’ Regular & ‘Masters Of The Universe’ Ally Was 94 Julianne Moore To Star In New Play ‘Faydra’ Off Broadway Tedde Moore Dies: Teacher In ‘A Christmas Story’ Who Had Dozens Of Other Credits Was 79 View All August 10, 2026 3:27pm Jon Cypher as Chief Daniels in 'Hill Street Blues' (1981-87) and as Man-at-Arms in 'Masters of the Universe' (1987) Everett Collection Jon Cypher , who played Chief Daniels in scores of Hill Street Blues episodes, was He-Man’s chief ally in 1987’s Masters of the Universe , starred on Major Dad and appeared in dozens of other TV series and films over nearly a half-century, died August 3 at his home in Central Point, Oregon. He was 94. His family told local news outlet Ashland News that he died with his wife by his side but did not reveal a cause of death. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries James B. Sikking Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’, ‘Doogie Howser, M.D.’ Actor Was 90 Cypher probably is best known for his role as the politics-savvy and sometimes duplicitous Police Chief Fletcher Daniels in more than 70 episodes of NBC’s 1980s cop drama Hill Street Blues from 1981-87. Although the series created by Steven Bochco-Michael Kozoll never was a big ratings hit — ranking only 27th among primetime series in its first season and never breaking the Top 20 in a three-network universe — its influence was undeniable as critics swooned. The series amassed 26 Emmys, dozens more nominations and was the first show to win four consecutive Emmys for Outstanding Drama Series, from 1981-84. During Hill Street ‘s run, Cypher was cast as He-Man key ally Duncan, aka Man-at-Arms, in the 1987 cult pic Masters of the Universe. Idris Elba plays the character in this year’s reboot starring Nicholas Galitzine. Another big role came around in 1990 when Cypher joined the CBS sitcom Major Dad as Brig. Gen. Marcus Craig for the show’s final three seasons into 1993. But those career-defining parts came a quarter-century or more into his acting career. Born on January 13, 1932, in New York City, Cypher’s first credit was playing Prince Christopher in CBS’ 1957 landmark live telecast of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s musical Cinderella , which starred Julie Andrews and drew more than 100 million U.S. viewers. He then played the first nine Broadway roles, starting with The Disenchanted and including such 1960s productions as The Night of the Iguana, Man of La Mancha, The Great White Hope and 1776 . His final Broadway credit was playing toy story owner Mr. MacMillan in the 1996 production of Big . In the early 1960s, he was cast in the single-season CBS daytime soap Our Five Daughters — which debuted a year after the sitcom My Three Sons — beginning a string of roles in serials for Cypher. He went on to appear on the likes of General Hospital, As the World Turns and Santa Barbara , along with primetime soaps Dynasty, Dallas and Knots Landing. Along the way, he guested on dozens of memorable TV hits from Mission: Impossible, Bonanza and The F.B.I. to The Rockford Files, The Love Boat and Knight Ryder to Hunter, The Commish, JAG, Law & Order, Walker, Texas Ranger and Murder, She Wrote. Cypher’s first big-screen credit was a starring role in 1971’s Valdez Is Coming, playing a powerful rancher who falsely accuses a man of murder and forces the town sheriff (Burt Lancaster) to kill the guy. When the lawman asks for compensation for the fallen man’s widow, Cypher’s Frank Tanner summons a force to battle him. Future Law & Order Emmy winner and DGA Lifetime Achievement Award winner Edwin Sherin directed the film. Cypher would appear in a number of other features during his long career, including Strictly Business and Off the Mark, but TV was his main medium. He also appeared in a number of telefilms such as Elvis & Me, Malice in Wonderland , Night Games and Juan Peron in Evita Peron . His final credit was playing a director in a pair of The Lot episodes in 2001. He also was a singer — his Ashland News obit noted that he sang opera in four languages — and was the author of a book of limericks titled If You’re Not Depressed, You Oughta Be in Therapy. Cypher is survived by his wife of 40 years, Carol Rosin. Information of other survivors was not available. He was to be buried at the Forest Conservation Burial Ground in Ashland, Oregon. title: Sony Pre-Empts ‘The Ballad Of The Ember Knight’; 14th Century-Set Spec By First-Time Scribes Lands Near 7-Figures
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Fleming Jr Mike Fleming Jr Editor-At-Large @DeadlineMike More Stories By Mike Sony Pre-Empts ‘The Ballad Of The Ember Knight’; 14th Century-Set Spec By First-Time Scribes Lands Near 7-Figures Netflix Plans Epic Survival Story Of Ernest Shackleton In Movie From ‘Adolescence’ Director Phil Barantini & ‘The Revenant’ Scribe Mark L. Smith AI Questions Spoil Book & Movie Heat On Unpublished Debut Novel ‘Call Me, I’ll Hide The Body’ – The Dish View All August 10, 2026 2:18pm L-R: Kieran O'Dea and Brennan O'Dea Courtesy photos EXCLUSIVE : After Christopher Nolan turned Homer’s ancient poem into gold with The Odyssey , maybe Hollywood is ready to take more chances on literate period fare. How else to explain the high level of interest when CAA and Kaplan Perrone went out with the spec script The Ballad of the Ember Knight , a 14th century-set drama that clocked in at 190 pages? When the dust settled, Sony paid near seven-figures to the sibling writing team Kieran and Brennan O’Dea. It is the first time they sold a script. Ember Knight is a medieval epic set against the French and English conflict during the Hundred Years’ War. The hero is a legendary warrior accused of murdering the royal family. To reclaim his standing, he must protect the kingdom’s last surviving prince from the conspiracy that threatens them both. Sony’s Brittany Morrissey and Peter Kang brought it into the studio, and it came without producer attachments. Related Stories Casting Uli Latukefu Lands Villain Role Of Ganondorf In Sony & Nintendo's 'The Legend Of Zelda' Movie News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swings To $42M Tuesday U.S. Box Office Record, Biggest Pic Global YTD With $1.1B How did this become the talk of town at a time when the material market goes into summer slumber? It started with Kaplan/Perrone, which was asked to read the script, knowing full well it would be a hard sell given its length. They flipped for it, CAA got into it, and they took it out. Watch on Deadline While there was flirtation with doing Ember as a longform TV effort because of its length and sweep, the scribes didn’t want to go that route. Nor did they want to cut their work down to the usual length of around 112 pages for a feature script. Sony moved quickly. Who are the O’Dea brothers? They are the middle sons of astronomers. Originally from the East Coast, they grew up in Baltimore and then Rochester before moving to northern Idaho after college. Their storytelling passion was fueled by their late grandfather, who would tell them as bedtime stories works like The Iliad, The Odyssey, Macbeth , WWII, and an errant knight named Sir Kay. It is comforting to know there is still a place for the classics in Hollywood. The brothers are repped by CAA and Kaplan Perrone. title: ‘Pluribus’ Duo Vince Gilligan And Composer Dave Porter On Long-Running Collaboration & That Addictive Main Theme – Crew Call Podcast
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Pluribus’ Duo Vince Gilligan And Composer Dave Porter On Long-Running Collaboration & That Addictive Main Theme – Crew Call Podcast ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Second-Fastest Film To Cross $1B At Int’l Box Office, With Global At $1.67B; ‘PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie’ Opens With $25M Summer Domestic Box Office On A Hot Streak, Will Cross $4B By Monday View All August 10, 2026 2:45pm L-R: Vince Gilligan and Dave Porter Apple TV Of the 18 Emmy nominations for Apple TV ‘s Pluribus , composer Dave Porter can call dibs on three of ’em: for Outstanding Music Composition for a Series, Sound Mixing for a Comedy or Drama Series (One Hour), and Original Main Title Theme Music. It’s a sweet moment for Porter, for after his 18-year collaboration with series creator Vince Gilligan on Breaking Bad, spinoff Better Call Saul and now Pluribus, the Television Academy has finally recognized his nuanced sound, which always pushes the boundary of not only score but also story. Related Stories News Cover Story: Rhea Seehorn Answers All The Big ‘Pluribus’ Questions – Will Carol Blow Up The World In Season 2? News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘Pluribus’ Helped Apple Land Record Emmy Noms, Apple’s Matt Cherniss Says “Quality Over Quantity” Strategy Is Paying Off We talk with the duo on the latest episode of Deadline’s Crew Call podcast about their roots together, their shorthand and philosophy on scoring, and how that 20-second, New Age, harmonized choral main title theme (or “ear wig,” as Gilligan calls it) came about. In that short time span, the music sets the table for the show’s trippy dystopian future where a woman is one of a few untouched survivors in a world where an extraterrestrial virus has turned the majority of Earth’s denizens into peaceful, hive-minded people. It’s no wonder that Porter started his professional career as an assistant to three-time Oscar-nominated minimalist film composer Philip Glass. Watch on Deadline Explains Porter about the melodic, two-part main title performed by Kenya Hathaway: “We’re presenting two sides of this argument. That’s the most interesting part of this show, is all the dichotomies that Vince has created here, and all the ways that we’re hopefully making our audience think and not take a side.” The composer adds, “We love to leave that ambiguity in there if we possibly can, because we want our audience to come to their own conclusions about this amazing world that Vince and our writers have created.” “These two vocal parts: sometimes they’re harmonious, sometimes they’re rubbing against each other in a discordant way, and they don’t seem to fit. And then ultimately, we’re leaving our audience there a little bit unsettled, but curious and hopefully humming a little too.” Says Gilligan about Porter: “[He asks], ‘How do you want the audience to feel? What’s the emotion you’re looking for?’ He always boils it down to that for me. And even then, which I always appreciate, he’s always throwing me a life preserver.” Below is our conversation; listen through to the end as Gilligan speculates how long he sees Pluribus lasting. title: Alexa Swinton, David Arquette, Wyatt Oleff & Sawyer Spielberg Set For Demolition Derby Drama ‘Wreckless’ From First-Time Feature Filmmaker Kayla Arend
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Nikki Glaser Signs With WME Alexa Swinton, David Arquette, Wyatt Oleff & Sawyer Spielberg Set For Demolition Derby Drama ‘Wreckless’ From First-Time Feature Filmmaker Kayla Arend CAA Signs Ashley Gill & Grant Gibbs Of Musical Comedy Duo A Twink And A Redhead View All August 10, 2026 2:55pm L-R: Alexa Swinton, David Arquette, Wyatt Oleff and Sawyer Spielberg Jonny Marlow/Ciaràn Maginn/Josh Katz/Bjorn Wallander EXCLUSIVE: Alexa Swinton ( Behemoth! ), David Arquette ( Scarpetta ), Wyatt Oleff ( It ) and Sawyer Spielberg ( Masters of the Air ) are underway on the Minnesota shoot for Wreckless , an indie sports drama marking the directorial debut of Kayla Arend , who’s working from a script she wrote with Mickey Falcone. Set within the male-dominated demolition derby community in rural Minnesota, Wreckless is a father-daughter story about addiction, grief and recovery centered on Joni (Swinton), a reckless teenager who has learned to live with pain, and her father Larry (Arquette), a recovering addict who has spent years trying to outrun his own mistakes. When Joni enters the demolition derby, the father and daughter are forced to confront the past and rebuild their relationship in the most unlikely of arenas. Related Stories Casting Mishka Sets Cast For Debut Feature 'My Boyfriend Is A Demon' Casting 'Scarpetta': David Arquette, Jodi Balfour, William Zabka, Kim Dickens, Killer Mike & Holland Taylor Among Season 2 Cast Additions The film is shooting amidst the real demolition derby community of Rochester, MN, with Oleff playing Atlas, Joni’s magnetic but troubled boyfriend, and Spielberg as Bo, Larry’s neighbor and sponsor. The cast also includes Rochester native Mohamed Khalid Mohamed as Ahmed, Joni’s best friend and co-worker, and other locals. Watch on Deadline A graduate of NYU’s Graduate Film program whose thesis film Leaving Yellowstone was executive produced by Spike Lee, Arend said: “This story is important to me as the child of a man who battled addiction. The unwavering support that I received from this community is something I am eternally grateful for and will never take for granted. I cannot fathom making this film anywhere else. Wreckless is very much a modern portrait of the Midwest that I know and love.” Cast by Barbara J. McCarthy ( Sovereign , Sitting in Bars with Cake ), Wreckless is executive produced by George Hubbard, Teresa Tsai, Timothy Carpenter, John Siff, Inna Swinton and Rolfe Swinton. Clément Bauer ( True Spirit , Sitting in Bars with Cake ), who’s producing for Resonate Entertainment alongside Vic Brandt ( She’s the He ), told us: “Kayla and I both grew up in this pocket of Minnesota, and we knew it was the only place to tell this story, not just to reflect on where we come from, but to shine a light on a community that rarely gets represented on screen.” Best known for roles on the shows And Just Like That… and Billions , Swinton’s film credits include M. Night Shyamalan’s Old , Bradley Cooper’s Maestro and Jake Schreier’s Marvel entry Thunderbolts *. Upcoming, she’ll be seen in Tony Gilroy’s Searchlight drama Behemoth! , set in the world of classical music, which is out December 4. She is repped by Osbrink, Untitled Entertainment and Lichter, Grossman, Nichols. Coming off an appearance in Scream 7 , Arquette’s upcoming slate includes Scarpetta Season 2 for Prime Video, as well as such indies as Wildcard , The Night Driver , The Mess We Made and Killing Hitler . He is repped by Artium and Lighthouse Entertainment. Most recently seen in Karate Kid: Legends and the Apple show City on Fire , Oleff’s also known for his work in the recent It films from New Line; the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise, where he played a young version of Chris Pratt’s Peter Quill; and the Netflix series I Am Not Okay with This . He is repped by Gersh, Untitled Entertainment and Myman Greenspan. Spielberg has appeared in the Apple series Masters of the Air , the Cannes-premiering Christmas Eve in Miller’s Point , A24’s Materialists from Celine Song, and more. He is repped by Swiontek Entertainment and Gang, Tyre, Ramer.
